sounds.name: Basic Patch
sounds.ref: The SYNTRX II manual’s first example patch (p. 19)
sounds.blurb: Oscillator 1’s two waves straight to an output: the smallest patch that makes a sound.
sounds.how: Nothing on the SYNTRX II is connected until you set a point in the matrix. This patch sets two: Oscillator 1’s pulse (row 1) and its sine (row 2) both into Ch1 Output (column A). Nothing shapes it, so it is a drone: it sounds all the time, and the keys only change its pitch.

steps.title: Oscillator 1’s pulse to channel 1
steps.why:
Set point A1: row 1, Oscillator 1’s pulse, into column A, Ch1 Output.
- Oscillator 1 pulse LEVEL 6: it sets how much of the pulse reaches row 1, wherever row 1 goes.
- Listen for: a hollow, buzzy square wave that never stops. The keys move its pitch.

steps.title: Add the sine
steps.why:
Set point A2: Oscillator 1’s sine (row 2) joins the pulse in column A. Points in one column mix.
- Oscillator 1 sine LEVEL 6.
- Listen for: the same note, rounder and fuller underneath.

steps.title: Shape both waves
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s SHAPE changes both waves at once: the pulse narrows and the sine bends into a sharkfin.
- SHAPE 3.
- Listen for: a thinner, nasal pulse and a brighter top to the sine.

context.osc1.pulse: In this sound: the pulse’s share of the drone.
context.osc1.shape: In this sound: 0 is a square and a pure sine; either way adds edge.

tweaks.hear: The sine turns into an upside-down sharkfin and the pulse goes thin and reedy.
The whole drone drops an octave.

sounds.name: Filtered Oscillator
sounds.ref: The SYNTRX II manual’s filter example (p. 19)
sounds.blurb: A pulse through the high-pass and low-pass filter, from bright and open to a narrow band.
sounds.how: Oscillator 1’s pulse goes into the filter (column G) and the filter’s output (row 10) to channel 1. The SYNTRX’s filter is a high-pass and a low-pass in a row: with HPF at 0 it is a low-pass, with LPF at 10 a high-pass, and between them a band-pass.

steps.title: Through the filter
steps.why:
Set point G1 (Oscillator 1 pulse into the Filter column) and A10 (the filter, row 10, into Ch1 Output).
- Oscillator 1 pulse LEVEL 6, filter LEVEL 8.
- LPF is at 10 and HPF at 0, so both filters are open.
- Listen for: the plain buzzy pulse, still a drone.

steps.title: Close the low-pass
steps.why:
Turn LPF down and RESONANCE up. Above the LPF setting the sound is cut away, and resonance rings at the cut-off.
- LPF 4, RESONANCE 5.
- Listen for: a darker, rounder note with a ring to it.

steps.title: Open the high-pass
steps.why:
Turn HPF up: now the bottom is cut away too, leaving a band in the middle.
- HPF 3.
- Listen for: a thin, nasal, telephone-like tone.

context.vcf.lpf: In this sound: the top of the band. Lower is darker.
context.vcf.hpf: In this sound: the bottom of the band. Higher is thinner.

tweaks.hear: The filter whistles a pure tone of its own over the pulse.
The bass comes back: a plain low-pass again.

sounds.name: Looping VCA
sounds.ref: The SYNTRX II manual’s trapezoid example (p. 20)
sounds.blurb: The trapezoid envelope looping on its own, pulsing the filtered oscillator in a steady rhythm.
sounds.how: The filtered pulse goes through the trapezoid’s own VCA (column D) and out from row 12. The trapezoid loops on its own while OFF is at 9 or below, so the sound pulses without a key: ATTACK, ON, DECAY and OFF set the rhythm.

steps.title: Filter into the VCA
steps.why:
Set points G1 (pulse into the filter), D10 (the filter into the Envelope Signal column, the VCA’s input) and A12 (the VCA, row 12, to Ch1 Output).
- Oscillator 1 pulse LEVEL 6, filter LEVEL 6, LPF 5, RESONANCE 3.
- SIGNAL 7: the trapezoid VCA’s level onto row 12.
- Listen for: a short note on each key, the trapezoid fired by the key.

steps.title: Let the trapezoid loop
steps.why:
Turn OFF down below 9: the trapezoid stops waiting for a key and cycles on its own, resting for the OFF time between each envelope.
- ATTACK 1, ON 2, DECAY 4, OFF 4.
- Listen for: a steady pulse, about four a second, that keeps going without a key.

context.trap.off: In this sound: the gap between pulses. Above 9 it stops looping.
context.trap.decay: In this sound: how long each pulse rings.

tweaks.hear: The pulses come much faster, nearly a buzz.
Each pulse swells in instead of starting with a click.

sounds.name: Keyboard Bass
sounds.ref: Classic technique: a mono synth patch made on the matrix
sounds.blurb: Oscillator 2 through the filter and the trapezoid’s VCA, with the trapezoid opening the filter: a playable bass.
sounds.how: This is the patch a fixed synth has built in, made by hand: oscillator → filter → VCA → output. The trapezoid waits for a key (OFF above 9) and also opens the filter, through the Filter Frequency column. Both oscillators already follow the keyboard; there is no keyboard row to patch.

steps.title: Oscillator 2, filter and VCA
steps.why:
Oscillator 2’s pulse and saw are mixed onto row 3. Set G3 (into the filter), D10 (the filter into the VCA) and A12 and C12 (the VCA to both output channels).
- Oscillator 2 saw LEVEL 7, OCTAVE −1.
- Filter LEVEL 7, LPF 3, RESONANCE 4. SIGNAL 7.
- Listen for: a short, dark note on each key.

steps.title: The trapezoid opens the filter
steps.why:
Set N11: the trapezoid’s voltage (row 11) into the Filter Frequency column. The HPF / LPF switch is at LPF, so it moves the low-pass.
- TRAPEZOID 4: how far it opens the filter.
- DECAY 3.5: the filter and the level fall together.
- Listen for: each note starting bright and closing quickly, the classic synth bass “pluck”.

steps.title: Add the pulse
steps.why:
Bring Oscillator 2’s pulse into its mix as well.
- Oscillator 2 pulse LEVEL 5, SHAPE 3 (a narrower pulse).
- Listen for: a thicker, hollower bass.

context.trap.level: In this sound: how far each note opens the filter.
context.vcf.lpf: In this sound: where the filter rests between notes.

tweaks.hear: Each note squelches as the filter sweeps down.
Longer notes that close more slowly.

sounds.name: Modulation Madness
sounds.ref: The SYNTRX II manual’s modulation example (p. 21)
sounds.blurb: The looping VCA patch, with Oscillator 3 sweeping the filter and the joystick bending pitch and pulse width.
sounds.how: Control voltages go into the matrix exactly as sounds do. Oscillator 3, slow, sweeps the filter; the joystick’s left-right voltage moves Oscillator 1’s pulse width through the Oscillator Shape column, and its up-down voltage moves Oscillator 1’s pitch.

steps.title: The looping VCA
steps.why:
As in Looping VCA: points G1, D10 and A12, with the trapezoid looping.
- Pulse LEVEL 6, filter LEVEL 6, LPF 4, RESONANCE 4, SIGNAL 7.
- ATTACK 1, ON 2, DECAY 4, OFF 4.
- Listen for: a steady pulse.

steps.title: Oscillator 3 sweeps the filter
steps.why:
Set N4: Oscillator 3’s triangle (row 4) into Filter Frequency.
- Oscillator 3 TUNE 3 (about 0.3 Hz), triangle LEVEL 6.
- Listen for: the pulses slowly growing brighter and darker.

steps.title: The joystick takes over
steps.why:
Set K16 (joystick left-right into Oscillator Shape, which moves Oscillator 1’s pulse width with OSC1 SHAPE at its centre) and H15 (joystick up-down into Oscillator 1’s pitch).
- ↔ LEVEL 6, ↕ LEVEL 2. The stick is set a little up and to the right.
- Listen for: a different pitch and a thinner pulse. Move the stick to play with both.

context.joy.x: In this sound: the pulse width of Oscillator 1.
context.joy.y: In this sound: Oscillator 1’s pitch, up or down.
context.osc3.tune: In this sound: how fast the filter sweeps.

tweaks.hear: The pitch dives.
The filter wobbles fast instead of sweeping.

sounds.name: Auto-Pan Through Input 2
sounds.ref: The SYNTRX II manual’s stereo panning example (p. 22)
sounds.blurb: A drone that swings between the speakers, using Input 2 to turn Oscillator 3 upside down.
sounds.how: Oscillator 1 goes to both channels, panned hard left and right. Oscillator 3 raises channel 1’s level; it also goes to the Scope column, and the SCOPE OUTPUT is normalled to Input 2. With Input 2 at INVERT its row carries Oscillator 3 upside down, which lowers channel 2 as channel 1 rises.

steps.title: One drone, two channels
steps.why:
Set A1 and C1: Oscillator 1’s pulse to both Ch1 Output and Ch2 Output.
- Pulse LEVEL 6.
- PAN channel 1 to −5 (left) and channel 2 to +5 (right). Both LEVELs at 5, halfway, so a voltage can move them either way.
- Listen for: the drone in both speakers.

steps.title: Oscillator 3 moves channel 1
steps.why:
Set O4: Oscillator 3’s triangle into Output ch. level 1.
- Oscillator 3 TUNE 3.5 (about half a cycle a second), triangle LEVEL 8.
- Listen for: the left side swelling and fading.

steps.title: Input 2 turns it over for channel 2
steps.why:
Set B4 (Oscillator 3 into the Scope column, and so into Input 2) and P9 (Input 2 into Output ch. level 2).
- Input 2 at LINE and INVERT, LEVEL 7.
- Listen for: the drone swinging from left to right and back.

context.in2.polarity: In this sound: INVERT is what makes channel 2 move against channel 1.
context.osc3.tune: In this sound: the speed of the swing.

tweaks.hear: Both sides now swell together: tremolo instead of panning.
A fast stereo shimmer.

sounds.name: Dry and Wet Delay
sounds.ref: The SYNTRX II manual’s effects example (p. 23)
sounds.blurb: Short notes with echoes: the effect only gives the wet sound, so the dry sound is patched alongside it.
sounds.how: Oscillator 1’s pulse goes through the trapezoid’s VCA to channel 1 (the dry sound) and to the Effects column. The effect’s output, row 14, is only the echoes, so it is patched to channel 1 too and EFFECTS LEVEL sets the mix.

steps.title: A short note
steps.why:
Set D1 (the pulse into the VCA) and A12 (the VCA to Ch1 Output).
- Pulse LEVEL 6, SIGNAL 7, DECAY 3.
- Listen for: short, plucked notes.

steps.title: Send it to the delay
steps.why:
Set F12 (the VCA into the Effects column) and A14 (the effect, row 14, to Ch1 Output).
- DELAY / REVERB at DELAY, TIME 6, FEEDBACK 5, LEVEL 6.
- Listen for: each note followed by fading repeats.

context.fx.level: In this sound: the wet share of the mix. The dry sound is set by SIGNAL.
context.fx.feedback: In this sound: how many echoes each note gets.

tweaks.hear: The echoes blur into a room around each note.
The echoes build on themselves and run away into a howl.

sounds.name: Ring Modulator Bells
sounds.ref: Classic technique: ring modulation for bell tones
sounds.blurb: Two oscillators multiplied in the ring modulator and given a long decay: metallic bells.
sounds.how: The ring modulator multiplies whatever is pinned into Ringmod A by the signal its SOURCE B switch picks inside the instrument, here Oscillator 2. Neither pitch survives, only their sum and difference, and when the two are not in a simple ratio the result rings like metal.

steps.title: Two oscillators in the ring modulator
steps.why:
Set E2: Oscillator 1’s sine into Ringmod A. SOURCE B is at OSC2, so Oscillator 2 is the other input. Then D13 (the ring modulator, row 13, into the VCA) and A12 and C12 (the VCA to both channels).
- Oscillator 1 sine LEVEL 7. Oscillator 2 saw LEVEL 6, OCTAVE +1, TUNE 6.4: out of a simple ratio with Oscillator 1.
- Ring LEVEL 7, SIGNAL 7.
- Listen for: a clangy, inharmonic tone on each key.

steps.title: A bell’s long decay
steps.why:
A bell is struck and rings away. The trapezoid stays up while a key is held, so strike the keys briefly.
- ATTACK 0, ON 0, DECAY 9.
- Listen for: bright strikes that fade over about a second.

steps.title: Some room
steps.why:
Set F12 and C14: the bell into the effects, the reverb onto channel 2.
- REVERB, TIME 6, FEEDBACK 5, LEVEL 5.
- Listen for: the bells ringing on in a space.

context.osc2.tune: In this sound: sets the bell’s metal. Small moves change the timbre completely.
context.trap.decay: In this sound: how long each bell rings.

tweaks.hear: A simple octave ratio: the clang becomes a hollow, nearly musical tone.
The bell dissolves into a crunchy, noisy hiss.

sounds.name: Random Bleeps
sounds.ref: Classic technique: sample and hold on pitch
sounds.blurb: Noise sampled and held, moving the pitch in random steps: the sound of a film computer thinking.
sounds.how: The sample and hold takes a value of whatever is pinned into its S&H Input column at each tick of S&H RATE and holds it. Fed noise, each value is random. Row 5 is shared with Oscillator 3’s pulse, so the OSC 3 / S&H switch puts the S&H on it, and row 5 goes to Oscillator 1’s pitch.

steps.title: A filtered tone
steps.why:
Set G2 (Oscillator 1’s sine into the filter) and A10 and C10 (the filter to both channels).
- Sine LEVEL 7, filter LEVEL 7, LPF 6, RESONANCE 6.
- Listen for: a steady tone.

steps.title: Noise into the sample and hold
steps.why:
Set M6 (noise into the S&H Input) and H5 (row 5 into Oscillator 1’s pitch). Switch OSC 3 / S&H to S&H.
- Noise LEVEL 6, S&H RATE 4 (about eight steps a second), S&H LEVEL 7.
- Listen for: the pitch jumping to a new random note eight times a second.

steps.title: The steps move the filter too
steps.why:
Set N5: the same random steps into Filter Frequency.
- Listen for: each new note brighter or duller than the last.

context.snh.rate: In this sound: how often the pitch jumps.
context.snh.level: In this sound: how far apart the random notes are.

tweaks.hear: A fast, chattering babble.
The notes stay close together: a gentle burble.

sounds.name: Super Saw Lead
sounds.ref: Classic technique: a thick, detuned saw lead
sounds.blurb: Oscillator 2’s saw turned into its “dual super saw”, with a little vibrato from Oscillator 3 and an echo.
sounds.how: Oscillator 2’s SHAPE does two things at once: it narrows the pulse and thickens the saw into a “dual super saw”, a second saw drifting out of tune against the first. Only the saw is used here, through the filter and the VCA.

steps.title: A saw lead
steps.why:
Set G3 (Oscillator 2 into the filter), D10 (the filter into the VCA) and A12 and C12 (to both channels).
- Oscillator 2 saw LEVEL 7, filter LEVEL 7, LPF 7, RESONANCE 2, SIGNAL 7, ON 3, DECAY 6.
- Listen for: a bright, plain saw note on each key.

steps.title: Make it super
steps.why:
Turn Oscillator 2’s SHAPE up.
- SHAPE 8.
- Listen for: the note thickening and shimmering as the second saw beats against the first.

steps.title: Vibrato and an echo
steps.why:
Set I4 (Oscillator 3’s triangle into Oscillator 2’s pitch, gently) and F12 and A14 (an echo on channel 1).
- Oscillator 3 TUNE 6 (about 5 Hz), triangle LEVEL 1.
- Effects TIME 5, FEEDBACK 3, LEVEL 4.
- Listen for: a singing vibrato and a soft echo behind each phrase.

context.osc2.shape: In this sound: how thick the super saw is.
context.osc3.tri: In this sound: the depth of the vibrato. A little goes a long way.

tweaks.hear: A single, thinner saw.
A softer, darker lead.

sounds.name: Sync Sweep
sounds.ref: Classic technique: a hard-sync lead swept by the envelope
sounds.blurb: Oscillator 2 hard-synced to Oscillator 1, its pitch swept by the trapezoid on every note: a tearing, vocal lead.
sounds.how: With SYNC on, Oscillator 2 restarts with every cycle of Oscillator 1, so the note you hear is Oscillator 1’s and changing Oscillator 2’s pitch changes its tone instead. The trapezoid, pinned into Oscillator 2’s frequency, sweeps that tone with each note.

steps.title: Oscillator 2 to the outputs
steps.why:
Set D3 (Oscillator 2 into the VCA) and A12 and C12 (to both channels).
- Oscillator 2 saw LEVEL 7, SIGNAL 7, ON 3, DECAY 6.
- Listen for: a plain saw note.

steps.title: Sync it to Oscillator 1
steps.why:
Switch SYNC to OSC2 → OSC1, and raise Oscillator 2 above Oscillator 1. Oscillator 1 is not patched anywhere, but it is still running, and now sets the pitch.
- SYNC on, Oscillator 2 OCTAVE +1, TUNE 6.
- Listen for: the same note, now with a hard, buzzing edge.

steps.title: Sweep it with the trapezoid
steps.why:
Set I11: the trapezoid into Oscillator 2’s frequency. Played from the keys, the trapezoid rises over ATTACK, holds while the key is down, and falls after it.
- TRAPEZOID 3, ATTACK 6.
- Listen for: each note tearing open as it starts, a vocal “yow”, and closing again as you let go.

context.trap.level: In this sound: how far each note sweeps.
context.osc2.tune: In this sound: where the sweep settles: the tone, not the pitch.

tweaks.hear: Oscillator 2’s own pitch swoops up and back on every note.
A wilder, longer sweep.

sounds.name: Looping Reverb Drone
sounds.ref: The SYNTRX II manual’s tip: the reverb at full FEEDBACK as a drone source
sounds.blurb: Short noise bursts into a reverb set to ring forever: a dark, breathing wash.
sounds.how: The manual points out that with FEEDBACK all the way up the reverb keeps going on its own and becomes a drone source. Here the looping trapezoid fires short bursts of filtered noise into it, and only the reverb, row 14, is heard.

steps.title: Bursts of noise
steps.why:
Set G6 (noise into the filter), D10 (the filter into the VCA) and F12 (the VCA into the effects). Set A14 and C14: only the effect is heard.
- Noise LEVEL 6, filter LEVEL 7, LPF 5, RESONANCE 5, SIGNAL 7.
- The trapezoid loops: ATTACK 0, ON 0, DECAY 2, OFF 6.
- REVERB, TIME 6, FEEDBACK 6, LEVEL 8.
- Listen for: soft, regular whooshes in a large room.

steps.title: Let it ring forever
steps.why:
Turn FEEDBACK all the way up: the reverb no longer dies away, so every burst adds to one continuous wash.
- FEEDBACK 10.
- Listen for: the room filling up into a dark, breathing drone.

context.fx.feedback: In this sound: at 10 the reverb never dies away.
context.trap.off: In this sound: the gap between bursts.

tweaks.hear: Brighter, hissier bursts and a lighter wash.
A huge room: the wash grows deeper and slower.
